reviews.outcome: Local boundary case [SMITH-01](source-errors/findings/SMITH-01.json). No serious defect was found in the earlier induction and primitive-recursion scopes. CRT needs an explicit coprime-cancellation lemma for self-contained use. Formalized Σ₁ completeness is sketched, not fully audited; Goodstein unprovability is not proved by its introduction.  No additional serious defect was found in the earlier arithmetic-entry scope. The corpus spells out a one-extra-point Q model and all multiplication cases; leaving operations as an exercise is not a source error. Its characteristic functions use 1 for true, unlike this source’s opposite convention.  Serious proof-checker defect [SMITH-02](source-errors/findings/SMITH-02.json), repaired by strictly smaller proof subcodes. The source’s Hilbert calculus and prime codes are not adopted; the corpus codes its existing natural-deduction rules and square-pair lists. The modulus-one repair in SMITH-01 is retained; coprime cancellation is supplied locally, with division reused from the existing corpus. Numeralwise uniqueness is distinguished from one uniform theorem of totality. No new serious mathematical defect was found in this selected scope.  No serious defect found in the selected diagonal and Tarski arguments. The corpus separates truth in the standard model from provability and does not import the surrounding incompleteness results or complexity-preserving claims. No serious defect found in these selected incompleteness arguments. The corpus uses its fixed-point equivalence proved already in true Q when claiming standard truth, and does not import Pi-one/Sigma-one complexity preservation. The checker repair SMITH-02 is retained in the existing coding. The source itself warns that arbitrary numeralwise representatives need not support the second derivability condition; the third-condition proof is only a sketch.
